newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: India looking at further economic steps - Fin Min.
newsitem.headline: India looking at further economic steps - Fin Min.

text.p: The Indian government will consider further economic measures, such as restructuring the coal industry, this month although strictly finance-linked steps will have to await the budget, Finance Minister P. Chidambaram told Reuters.
"Some issues are under consideration. There is a whole policy paper on restructuring the coal industry that is under consideration.
"Various other issues will also be considered by the cabinet...but I cannot say what they are because they have financial implications," he said on the fringes of the World Economic Forum.

Indian shares tumbled on Friday after the government dashed investor hopes of a new package of measures to boost capital markets. It said that the expected package was actually measures already taken since January.
In an interview with Reuters Financial Television, Chidambaram said that he was confident that India could still meet its five percent inflation target for the April-March financial year.
"As of now, I am confident that we will be more or less on target for five percent," he said.
"Next year, we hope we can make a significant further correction," he said.
He said in the interview that the recent opening up of the gilt market to foreign investors should help to bring down interest rates further.
